<thought>To propose a single‑step retrosynthesis we need a reaction that can form the bicyclic core of the target in one transformation. The target SMILES  
`COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O`  
contains a cyclohexene fused to a cyclopentane ring and a bridgehead carbon bearing a methyl ester. This pattern is classic for a Diels‑Alder cycloaddition: the two new σ‑bonds created in the forward reaction correspond to the formation of a six‑membered ring from a conjugated diene and a dienophile (an α,β‑unsaturated carbonyl).  

Thus the retrosynthetic step is a single Diels‑Alder reaction that disconnects the two bonds formed in the cycloaddition, giving a diene fragment and a dienophile fragment. I will search the template catalog for a Diels‑Alder type template (bonds formed “6-6” and bond order change “6-6 (2.0->1.0)”). Then I will use that template ID in the JSON route.
